provenance: All heating-on/off comparisons use identical irradiated original synthetic data, errors, physical candidate, phases/reducers and finite geometry. Two preliminary CPU unheated-model profiles generated their own unheated data and are excluded. The first two hardware correctness units and the two heated CPU fine profiles predate the observational-fixture correction. Their scientific kernel hashes match the final implementation.

The original independent CPU equations on this finite geometry run serially with vectorized NumPy. Reference and JAX CPU are distinct. Each measured candidate includes two fresh parameter-dependent finite fields and light curves, original normalization/third light/noise/prior/density and accuracy checks. Transfers, synchronization and host outputs are included. Timings of nested stages overlap.

Fine reference and extra correctness cases use CPU cores16–19, nice19. Matched benchmark processes use affinity0–15 nice10, BLAS/OMP single thread. Some private CPU validation and GPU units overlapped. Small samples, changed-shape compilation and profiling overhead limit timing interpretation.

Fine profiles include component, raw and normalized curves for both field levels and original observations. Timing series include original physical inputs, predictions, densities, finite metadata, all-curve and adaptive-trace hashes. Per-band irradiation differences are finite model responses that include spectral and normalization changes. Signed terms can cancel; strict acceptance uses component envelopes.
A notebook on the earlier m019 revision is available. Execution on a real Colab runtime and qualified checkpointable physical chains/ESS remain pending.
